clue.text: Recess (holy apse) fashioned on unknown pair of pieces linking bones in column

definitions.text: of pieces linking bones in column

parts.note: two algebraic unknowns, the last letters of the alphabet

indicators.note: something fashioned has been shaped anew, so the bracketed words are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: a recess is a gap or opening
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A church alcove is being built beside a pair of anatomical pieces in a spinal column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' and 'apse' both suggest church architecture, but only the bracketed words are rearranged; the recess itself stays intact.
explanation.definitionFit: Zygapophyses are the articulating processes that join adjacent vertebrae, and the adjective describes anything relating to them.

clue.text: Share of nearly all booze pronounced dodgy

definitions.note: loose: the answer is a security rather than strictly a share

indicators.note: nearly all of a word means its final letter is dropped
something dodgy is unreliable and out of true, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word with its last letter cut
taken as written, joining the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone takes a share of nearly all the drink, and the result is declared suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' looks like a homophone signal but is simply fodder for the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A zero-coupon bond is a tradable financial security paying no interest, sold at a discount, broadly a holding like a share.

clue.text: Get pasty and bloomer that's hand-picked for chain in north?

definitions.text: bloomer that's hand-picked for chain in north?

parts.note: to get (pale, say) is to go that way
pasty-faced means pale

explanation.surface: Someone turns pale, and a pasty and a loaf get picked for a shop chain up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' and 'bloomer' pose as bakery items; a bloomer is also a loaf, but here it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Gowan is the Scots word for a daisy, the flower children pick to thread into daisy chains.

clue.text: Mentally ready to have old Englishman immigrant replace university's late guide

indicators.note: to replace something is to take its place, so the newcomer goes where the university letter was

parts.note: to psych up is to get mentally ready
standard abbreviation for old
Pom is Australian slang for an English immigrant
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A psychologically prepared old English migrant takes over a university's guide.
explanation.walkthrough: PSYCH(U)P with O + POM in place of the U gives PSYCHOPOMP. 'Late' means dead, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychopomp, such as Hermes, conducts the souls of the dead to the underworld, so it guides the deceased.

clue.text: Normal, some claim ultimately, to get it for sex, say

parts.note: par is the normal standard
some, as in 'have you any?'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter of claim is used

parts.note: the final letter of claim

explanation.surface: Some argue it is normal to get it for sex, a remark about everyday behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR + ANY + M. The definition is an example: saying 'it' instead of 'sex' is such a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A paranym is a word whose meaning is twisted to disguise something, as when a coy euphemism stands in for a blunt one.

clue.text: Hospital area transport turning up at least sixteen miles from Kolkata?

definitions.text: at least sixteen miles from Kolkata?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up makes the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: short for sanatorium
standard abbreviation for area
a transport of delight is joy

explanation.surface: Hospital transport turns up after a long journey from Kolkata.
explanation.walkthrough: SAN + A + JOY reversed gives YOJANAS. 'Transport' is a feeling, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A yojana is an old Indian measure of distance of several miles, so a plural of them covers a good many.

clue.text: Old poet's child's play partially upset playwright aesthetically

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the letters upside down
partially means only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters spanning the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A playwright with aesthetic leanings is upset by a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: Spenser is the usual 'old poet', and his archaisms are fair game in barred puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Eath is an archaic word meaning easy, and child's play is an idiom for anything effortless.

clue.text: That can be raised with minimum of effort in set of stats

indicators.note: in places the chosen letter inside the other word

parts.note: something that can be lifted

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest bit, its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of effort

explanation.surface: Something that can be lifted with little effort features in a collection of statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: LIF(E)TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A life table is an actuarial chart giving mortality and survival figures by age.

clue.text: Old John's in colourful slip for tri-weekly exercises with large daughter

indicators.note: exercises work things vigorously, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
standard abbreviation for large
standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone called John wears a bright slip to do workouts three times a week with a big daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Old John is John Milton, who wrote of 'flowery-kirtled Naiades'; the word is his coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: A kirtle is a skirt or gown, so Milton's compound describes nymphs wearing floral-patterned skirts.

clue.text: Old explorer spoken of harshly

indicators.note: spoken of means we hear the name said, not see it spelt

parts.note: Sir Walter Raleigh, Elizabethan explorer

explanation.surface: A historic explorer is talked about in unkind terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Raleigh's name was pronounced like the adverb, which spells it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawly means in a crude, rough or cruel way, matching a severe, unkind manner.

clue.text: Abandoned Jesuit, Irish, travelling west, having acquired a fare from Indonesia

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means moving right to left
having acquired something means taking it in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: left behind
SJ, Society of Jesus, follows a Jesuit's name
standard abbreviation for Irish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lapsed Irish Jesuit heads west and picks up a dish from Indonesia on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' looks like an anagram signal, but it is simply LEFT. The definition here includes its article, 'a fare'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rijstafel is a Dutch-Indonesian rice table: a banquet of many small dishes served with rice.

clue.text: Walk in the park and round square that helps malaria sufferers

parts.note: something very easy
round in shape, like the letter
nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: A stroll in the park and round a square for those suffering from malaria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk in the park' and 'square' paint a town stroll; both are idioms and numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinchonine is an alkaloid from cinchona bark, related to quinine and used against the fever.

clue.text: Took in Perth, Western Australia, returning by steamboat after vacation

indicators.note: vacating empties a place, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the word emptied of its middle

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: the state's abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone took a steamboat to Perth in Western Australia and came back.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth is the Scottish city, not the Australian one: 'staw' is a Scots past tense of steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Staw is a Scots form meaning stole, so in Scottish speech it means pinched or nicked.

clue.text: Big fan of Rick Parfitt & co keeping third son in shelter across pond

parts.note: Rick Parfitt played guitar in the British rock band Status Quo

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the son goes within

parts.note: an enthusiast, as in fitness nut
Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: A devoted Status Quo fan shelters a youngest boy in America.
explanation.walkthrough: QUO + N(SETH)UT. 'Across pond' means in the US, over the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Quonset hut is the American semicircular prefabricated building of corrugated steel, much like a Nissen hut.

clue.text: Pancake Tuesday's first light snacks mostly filling I'm thinking

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so a final letter is dropped
filling something means going inside it

parts.note: the noise someone makes while pondering
tapas are light Spanish snacks, shortened by one letter

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of Tuesday

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: On Pancake Tuesday, someone wonders aloud about filling up on light snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: U(T + TAPA)M. 'Pancake Tuesday' looks like one phrase but splits: the pancake is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttapam is a thick South Indian griddle cake of fermented rice and lentil batter, a savoury flapjack.

clue.text: Rosyth's hesitant Romeo sailor in the red trousers

indicators.note: used as a verb, trousers means pockets, so one letter is taken inside

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
in debt
R is Romeo in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A shy lover from Rosyth, a sailor in scarlet trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: A sailor in the red (TAR + OWING) pockets R. Rosyth, a Scottish naval base, flags a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarrow is Scots for to delay or be reluctant, so tarrowing means holding back.

clue.text: Dung that is a brown colour

parts.note: sc, short for scilicet, means 'that is to say'
umber is an earthy brown pigment

explanation.surface: A blunt description of dung's brownish shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Scumber is an old word for the droppings of a fox or dog, animal excrement.

clue.text: Employee on croft, perhaps with duck was quick to corner sheep

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket

indicators.note: cornering something hems it in, so the animal is enclosed

parts.note: moved fast
a male sheep

explanation.surface: A crofter's worker hurries, with a duck, to round up a sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: O + R(RAM)AN. A croft is a small Scottish tenant farm, hinting at a Scots term.
explanation.definitionFit: An orra man is a Scots farm odd-job labourer, doing whatever tasks a small holding needs.

clue.text: Letter's discriminatory notice once, evoking certain pictures

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the '...' signs British landlords once put in windows
second meaning: suggestive of film noir

explanation.walkthrough: A 'letter' is one who lets rooms, a landlord; read as two words the answer is NO IRISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Noirish describes something reminiscent of the dark, cynical crime movies of 1940s Hollywood.

clue.text: Short story reflected top barrister's violent struggle in the past

parts.note: a conte is a short tale

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the abbreviation reads backwards

parts.note: a King's Counsel is a senior barrister

explanation.surface: A brief tale mirrored a leading lawyer's bitter fight of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Conteck is an archaic word for strife, quarrelling or contention, so a bygone fight.

clue.text: Translation of hoc, say — one making Latin blossom

indicators.note: translating changes words into another form, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Translating the Latin word hoc turns into a flowering of the language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' means Latin American: the shrub comes from Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Choisya is the Mexican orange shrub, prized for fragrant white flowers, so a flower from Latin America.

clue.text: Bore in Glasgow bar reeling off Genesis's number ones

indicators.note: number ones are the first in line, so only the initial letters count

parts.note: the initials of the four words

explanation.surface: A tedious man in a Glasgow pub churns out the band Genesis's chart hits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person; it is the verb, and Glasgow flags a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Brog is Scots for an awl or to prick with one, so to make a hole.

clue.text: Spinner putting pronounced damper on too-good-to-be-true run out

indicators.note: in an across entry, putting one thing on another places it after, so the damper goes last

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means sanctimonious
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: pronounced means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: damper means more wet, said as the end of the word

explanation.surface: A bowler puts a damper on a run out that seemed too good to be true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' and 'run out' suggest cricket; the spinner is a dancer. PI + RO + UETTER, said 'piro-wetter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouetter is someone who spins on one foot, as a ballet dancer twirls on point.

clue.text: Old pack: presumably not the only member of rowdy one to show up?

indicators.note: in a down entry, showing up means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.words: presumably not the only member of rowdy one
parts.note: a co-rat would be a fellow member of the Rat Pack, the hard-living Sinatra set; 'one' means pack

explanation.surface: An old gang whose members, presumably, all turned up together.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful coinage CO-RAT, a fellow rat, rests on the rowdy Rat Pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Taroc is an old name for tarot cards and the game played with that deck.

clue.text: Uneven contributions from emcee ruin failing club Down Under

indicators.note: uneven contributions are the odd-numbered letters of the words that follow
failing says those odd contributions drop out, leaving every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A compere's ruinous patchy contributions are sinking an Australian club.
explanation.walkthrough: Down Under suggests Australia, but the club is a New Zealand weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A meri is a short flat Maori war weapon of greenstone, so a cudgel from New Zealand.

clue.text: Eastern airline's ruined: their output took a hammering

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so its letters fall apart and are rearranged

parts.note: standard abbreviation for east
the possessive gives the final S

explanation.surface: An eastern carrier is in ruins: its business took a battering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took a hammering' sounds like failure; the products were literally hammered in.
explanation.definitionFit: Naileries are factories making nails, whose products are driven in with hammers.

clue.text: For singing in cathedral, maybe, with chapter out of hours

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: relating to a choir
standard abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: Cathedral singing goes on, with the chapter absent outside service hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of hours' reads as one phrase, but 'out' is the deletion and 'of hours' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Horal is an adjective relating to clock time, from Latin hora, so pertaining to the hour.

clue.text: Longed to ditch English after great hosts help to restore places for native tongue

indicators.note: a host holds guests inside, so the pair of letters goes around the helping words

parts.note: GT is an abbreviation for great
assistance
to make well again

indicators.note: to ditch something is to discard it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: yearned
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Nostalgic exiles drop English and seek help in reviving the old language's heartlands.
explanation.walkthrough: GT is a dictionary abbreviation for great, so it can wrap around the two helping words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gàidhealtachd is the Gaelic-speaking region of the Scottish Highlands and Islands.
